evals.name: A-marketplace
evals.prompt: Design the web app for Pasarloka, a consumer marketplace for Indonesian independent craft sellers (batik, ceramics, woodwork). Buyers mostly use Tokopedia and Shopee today. We want it to feel like its own brand, not a clone.
expectations: Names Tokopedia/Shopee (or similar) as the reference set and extracts their mental model
Search with autocomplete is visible in the header on every page
Category navigation and a product results grid with filters (as removable chips) and sort
Product page keeps gallery, price, variants, seller card and reviews
Cart grouped by seller and a standard checkout order (address, shipping, voucher, payment, review)
Recognises regional conventions such as chat with seller, vouchers, e-wallet/COD payments
Identity levers derived from the craft subject and explicitly avoids copying Shopee/Tokopedia visual identity
Does not replace core shopping flows with novel discovery patterns without justification

evals.name: B-inventory
evals.prompt: Build the main screen of an inventory management app for a warehouse team (5-20 operators, used all day). ~40k SKUs across 3 warehouses. They filter, sort, adjust stock in bulk and export.
expectations: Classifies the surface as high-frequency, expert, dense, and chooses a receding posture
Uses a dense sortable table rather than cards, with sticky header and tabular numerals
Includes row selection with bulk actions (adjust, transfer, export) and saved filters
Handles scale (virtualisation or server pagination with counts)
Stock status conveyed with icon/text plus colour, not colour alone
Explicitly avoids decorative motion, display fonts in data and decorative charts above the table

evals.name: C-analytics
evals.prompt: Design a product analytics app for a subscription business: MRR, churn, cohorts, funnel conversion, by plan and region. Used by growth PMs daily and by execs in a weekly review.
expectations: Global date range with comparison period and filters persisted in URL
Chart choice justified per analytical question (line for trends, cohort heatmap/table, funnel with drop-off, sorted bars for breakdowns)
KPI tiles show value, delta and comparison period
Drill-down from charts to underlying tables and metric definitions available
Distinguishes PM exploration from exec weekly-review needs
Avoids pie charts with many slices, 3D/gradient charts and neon mission-control styling

evals.name: D-landing
evals.prompt: Create the landing page for Driftnote, a tool that turns meeting recordings into decision logs for engineering teams.
expectations: Classifies as a persuasion surface with a step-forward posture
Identity levers are specific to the subject (decisions, records, engineering) rather than generic SaaS
Hero shows the real product output (a decision log) rather than abstract visuals
Explicitly avoids the generic template (gradient hero, three icon cards, buzzword copy)
Keeps conventional navigation, clear primary CTA and findable pricing; no scroll-jacking

evals.name: E-devtool
evals.prompt: Design the deployments page of a self-hosted PaaS: list of deployments, build logs, environment variables, and service settings.
expectations: Names developer-tool reference products (e.g. Vercel, Netlify, Render, Heroku)
Monospace for SHAs/logs/IDs with copy affordances
Logs with level filter, search, follow/tail, absolute timestamps and permalinks
Env vars masked with reveal/copy and diff or review before apply
High density with keyboard shortcuts or a command palette
Deep links to deployments/log lines and a danger zone with confirmation for destructive settings

evals.name: F-creative
evals.prompt: Design a tool for choreographers to compose dance sequences: arrange moves for multiple dancers over music, with formations on a stage.
expectations: Recognises no established convention fits and rejects a form/table-only approach
Proposes a bespoke core interaction (stage canvas + music timeline with keyframed formations and scrubbing)
Keeps the frame conventional: projects, undo/redo, autosave, export, inspector, shortcuts
Addresses discoverability and keyboard/accessibility for the bespoke interactions
Covers both parts of the brief: a move library/per-dancer move sequencing AND stage formations

evals.name: G-reject-novelty
evals.prompt: For our grocery delivery app, replace the product list and cart with a conversational AI chat as the only way to shop — it'll be more innovative.
expectations: States the cost of replacing habitual browse/cart infrastructure in a few sentences
Proposes chat as an accelerator on top of the conventional catalogue and visible cart
Respects user authority: will build chat-first if the user insists, keeping a visible basket

evals.name: H-reject-conventional
evals.prompt: Build a seating-plan tool for wedding planners. Just make it a standard admin CRUD: tables list, guests list, assign guest to table via a dropdown.
expectations: Identifies seating as a spatial, constraint-heavy task where CRUD mismatches the workflow
Proposes a floor-plan canvas with drag-and-drop plus a list view for search/bulk work, with conflict and capacity indicators
Advocates the spatial design concretely (flow or phased plan), then defers to the user's decision rather than conceding upfront

evals.name: I-existing-project
evals.prompt: (Repo uses shadcn/ui and Tailwind tokens.) Add a billing page; the current UI is bland, make this page stand out.
expectations: Inspects the existing project (components, tokens, layout shell) before designing
Uses existing primitives and tokens rather than a parallel component set or off-system colours
Achieves distinctiveness through composition and hierarchy within the system
Proposes system-level token changes if the system is genuinely lacking

evals.name: J-hybrid
evals.prompt: We're a B2B fleet-tracking SaaS. We need: marketing homepage, signup + onboarding, the live map/operations console, and account settings.
expectations: Assigns a separate posture to each surface based on signals
Operations console recedes: map plus list, prioritised alerts, density
Marketing steps forward and shows the real console
Explains coherence through shared tokens, voice and component behaviour
